video_directives: Trim the static holds at 10–13s (ear card) and 14–16s (ship card) by ~20% — the shockwave overlay repeats without new information
Give the 0–3s hook a faster title beat-in; two-line reveal reads slightly slow for a Short opening
Keep the looping character reactions (pose/expression shifts per beat) — this is the strongest life signal; add one more mid-frame blink pass to the static gauge section

top3_directives: Add a subtle rim-light or stronger silhouette edge to the volcano so it separates from the dark horizon band instead of blending into it
Push the smoke plume puffs with slightly more opacity/edge definition — they currently read as faint blobs and waste the upper-middle zone
Introduce one accent color (e.g., ember orange) echoed from the crater into the title or ring lines to tie foreground and background into one palette system
Clarify JAVA/SUMATRA labels — they float ambiguous over the horizon; anchor each to a visible landmass or connector so geography reads instantly
Fill the lower third dead zone: water is nearly empty below the character — add subtle wave animation or a glow path leading from character to volcano
Reposition the character so its pointing gesture actually aims at the volcano/1883 badge — currently the arm points off-frame left, breaking the intended eye path
Fix the character's pointing arm colliding with the 'DO' glyph — add padding or reposition the figure left so the gesture reads without touching the text block
Ground the stick figure: its shadow is barely visible and it floats against the dark blue band — deepen the contact shadow to anchor it

The volcano's white sticker-outline edge cuts off abruptly at the horizontal band line — either extend the eruption glow past the seam or add a subtle light spill so the split-screen transition feels intentional
Character in lower-left is dim and reads as clutter against the wave rings — raise its rim-light or scale it 15% to justify its presence
The gauge dial interior is a large flat navy void — add a subtle tick-label arc or inner shadow to give the focal element depth
Sound-wave rings in the lower-right are faint and clip awkwardly off-frame — commit to them with slightly stronger opacity or crop them deliberately
Lift the bottom scene out of the dark: the wincing character and ground are nearly crushed to black on a phone in daylight — add rim light or raise ambient exposure
Enlarge/bolden the '130 dB = PAIN' caption and add a subtle dark backing or stroke — it currently floats small against the gradient seam and could wash out
Fill the bottom-right dead zone: two-thirds of the lower panel is empty water — shift the character rightward or add a light prop/echo ripple to balance the ear's left-weighted composition
Character in bottom-left is dark-on-dark and tiny — rim-light it brighter or enlarge so it reads as the emotional focal point on a 6-inch screen
Bottom third of the water is a large near-black dead zone — add subtle wave highlights or a glow reflection from the ship window to fill it
Push the focal competition: rays + ship + character all fight equally; dim the rays slightly or add a glow behind the character so the eye path resolves
The top ~30% of the frame is a dead zone of near-black starfield with faint blob shapes — push the horizon/sun composition up or add a moon/cloud layer to occupy it
Palm silhouettes and debris island in the mid-right vanish against the purple — lighten them or add a rim glow so they read on a 6-inch daylight screen
'BOOM' and the '3,000 MILES AWAY' chip sit on opposite sides with nothing connecting them — align BOOM onto the arc's axis or tilt it toward the focal path to unify the two text moments
Boost the character's rim light or add a subtle local glow — he nearly vanishes against the near-black lower third on a daylight phone screen
The bottom-right two-thirds is a dead zone; either crop the composition tighter or add a faint ground/atmosphere gradient to carry the eye from planet to character
The teal ring line passes in front of AND behind the planet ambiguously at the right edge — clarify occlusion so the orbit reads as 3D

The caption block sits directly on high-detail white wave foam — add a stronger scrim/darkening behind 'THE SEA TOOK THEM' or shift the whole text stack down into the flatter dark water zone for guaranteed daylight legibility.

Upper ~35% of frame is near-empty dark purple sky with a faint moon — either push the wave taller, add subtle atmospheric layers (stars, cloud silhouettes), or crop framing tighter to kill the dead zone.

The hooded character reads as a pasted sticker: unify lighting with a cool blue/purple rim light matching the scene, ground it with a contact shadow, and align its glow temperature with the moon palette.
Fill the top-third starfield dead zone with a subtle moon or drifting smoke plume to complete the eye path from text to character
Increase 'GONE.' stroke/drop-shadow weight so it fully separates from the bright volcano-glow bloom behind it
Tighten the decorative circle so it frames both the character and text peak intentionally — currently it clips ambiguously through the water line
Fill the top ~35% dead zone: enlarge the moon, add drifting ash-cloud shapes or rising ember particles so the upper frame earns its space
Create an explicit eye path from the character's pointing arm to the volcano/text — the gesture currently points into empty water; reposition character or angle the arm toward the peak

Tighten the label system: merge 'ANAK KRAKATAU' and its translation into one badge with a subtitle line, and lift both slightly above the horizon line so they don't sit on the volcano's mid-slope seam
Character is small and anchored bottom-left; consider enlarging ~20% and rotating pose toward the volcano for a stronger eye-path read
